transcript: It is not normal to feel bloated all the time. If you wake up bloated, eat a meal and feel bloated, or constantly deal with gas and discomfort, your body may be trying to tell you something. I once worked with a woman who had struggled with bloating for years. She wasn't hungry in the morning, she skipped meals. When she did eat, she felt heavy and uncomfortable. She had also been constipated for most of her life. But the real problem wasn't just her gut, it was her nervous system. She lived in a constant state of stress. Certain conversations, people and situations would leave her feeling tense, anxious and overwhelmed. Her body was spending most of the day in fight or flight mode. When this happens, the body shifts energy away from digestion. Blood flow moves to the muscles and brain instead of the gut. So we focused on two simple things. First, breathing. Just 10 minutes in the morning and 10 minutes at night to help calm the nervous system. Second, bitters before meals. Dark greens, dark chocolate or a few drops of a bitter tincture. Bitter foods help activate the vagus nerve and support healthy digestion. Within a few weeks, her bloating improved, her digestion became more regular, her energy increased and she finally started feeling better. And if you're struggling with bloating, one thing I personally like to take is a quality fiber supplement. You can find the fiber I recommend on Amazon or in the link on my profile.
